name: @kitchensink/infra-global

scripts.deploy: npm run bundle:lambda && cdk deploy --app 'npx tsx bin/app.ts'

//: ⛔ NOT AN npm WORKSPACE. Infra installs on its own: workspaces exist to install the application together,
and a CDK app is not part of the application. Keeping it here dragged 149 MB of aws-cdk-lib into the root
tree, where `turbo prune` found it and shipped it inside every service image.
⚠️ The 14 `@kitchensink/*` packages this imports are deliberately NOT DECLARED. They are
unpublished workspace packages; declaring them would make `npm install` here resolve them from the registry
and 404. Node finds them by walking up to the repo root, where the workspace links live. Phantom
dependencies, recorded rather than left for the next reader to hit as a failing install.
⚠️ `@radicle-co/infra-shared` is pinned EXACTLY, not by range: a caret never resolves a prerelease, and CI
publishes prereleases. ⛔ The pipeline does NOT rewrite this value (owner ruling) — the version a build
uses is the one committed here, so what CI builds is what the diff says it builds. Moving it is a commit.
⛔ `zod` and `@nestjs/common` are IMPORTED but deliberately NOT DECLARED, on top of the workspace packages
above. They are the two libraries whose TYPES cross the boundary: these guards compare zod schemas and Nest
exceptions built by workspace code, and a second copy makes `tsc` reject the comparison outright ("Types
have separate declarations of a private property"). Undeclared, they resolve upward to the single root copy.
⚠️ The tests still PASS with a split copy — vitest resolves per module, `tsc` typechecks one program — so
only the typecheck catches it. That asymmetry is why this is written down rather than left to be
rediscovered by whoever next adds a shared library here.
